anomalies.observed: In the POWER TRAIN block the high-side 'Reverse polarity protection' switch T4 is an AON6407 MOSFET whose gate (pin 4) is referenced to GND through D1 (12 V zener) and R19 (33 k), i.e. a gate-to-ground high-side topology. The specification explicitly defines AON6407 as an N-channel MOSFET ('T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET)') and notes that r1 used a P-channel SI2301 for this exact role, while r2's discrete set does not contain any P-channel device.
anomalies.expected: A high-side reverse-polarity switch with the gate tied to ground requires a P-channel MOSFET (source on the output side, body diode oriented input→output, Vgs negative to turn on). An N-channel device in this position cannot turn on (gate at 0 V vs source at +24 V gives Vgs ≈ −24 V, which is both off and beyond the Vgs rating), so the 24 V rail would only pass through the body diode (or not at all) and the gate would be over-stressed.
